description: issue #673: `who` (Sprites, R/0->turtle) reports the current turtle, which at top level (no `tell`/`ask`/`each`, all SP2+) is the single default main turtle. `who` equals `first turtles` because both denote the main turtle and turtle `==` compares the stable id (C3), not the JS wrapper instance. The comparison is written directly as `print who == first turtles`: a zero-arg reporter is a valid left operand of `==`. (The *parenthesized* form `(who == first turtles)` reports `ol-bad-token` instead, because with a callable-name at the head the parser resolves `( ... )` as a `parenthesized-call` (spec/grammar.md:211) -- `who` called with args `== first turtles` -- not as a `parenthesized-expression` (spec/grammar.md:209); the direct form avoids that disambiguation entirely.)
